202	            mediaType: .video, outputSettings: try Self.videoSettings(settings, canvas: canvas))
203	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false

205	            throw Exporter.ExportError.presetUnavailable(Self.presetName(settings))

214	    /// The audio half: every composition audio track through the plan's mix.
215	    ///
216	    /// **`addAudioOutput`'s `audioMix` line is where the preview and the file
217	    /// agree about sound.**
218	    /// The mix carries the plan's volume envelope AND, for any track whose
219	    /// clips use pan, the compressor or noise reduction, the
220	    /// `MTAudioProcessingTap` that runs them (`AudioTap.swift`). Those taps
221	    /// were long believed to be an AVPlayer-only feature — true of the
222	    /// `AVAssetExportSession` this pipeline replaced, and the reason the
223	    /// effects were left unimplemented — but measured against
224	    /// `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` they run here as well: a tap that
225	    /// silenced its buffers produced a silent file, one tap per track saw only
226	    /// its own track, and with `reader.timeRange` set for an in/out export the
227	    /// tap is handed COMPOSITION time, so a clip's settings still line up with
228	    /// the clip. Nothing had to be re-implemented for the export; the DSP has
229	    /// one implementation and this reads through it.
230	    ///
231	    /// The one thing the file and the preview do not share is the reducer's
232	    /// 512-sample delay on a track that uses it, which both paths have and
233	    /// neither compensates: 10.7 ms of audio lag at 48 kHz, well inside every
234	    /// A/V sync tolerance, on tracks the user asked to clean.
235	    ///
236	    /// A timeline with no audio at all is not an error — it is a silent
237	    /// movie, and the track is simply not added. It IS an error when the
238	    /// preset writes nothing else.
239	    ///
240	    /// This adds the writer INPUT only. The reader output is added by `start`
241	    /// (`addAudioOutput`), because its format depends on the gain, which
242	    /// arrives after `init`.
243	    private func addAudio(settings: ExportSettings) throws {
244	        let tracks = built.composition.tracks(withMediaType: .audio)
245	        guard !tracks.isEmpty else {
246	            if settings.isAudioOnly { throw Exporter.ExportError.emptyTimeline }
247	            return
248	        }
249	        let input = AVAssetWriterInput(
250	            mediaType: .audio, outputSettings: Self.audioSettings(settings))
251	        input.expectsMediaDataInRealTime = false
252	        guard writer.canAdd(input) else {
253	            throw Exporter.ExportError.presetUnavailable(Self.presetName(settings))
254	        }
255	        writer.add(input)
256	        audioInput = input
257	    }
258	
259	    /// The mix's reader output (`audioReadOutput`). False when the reader
260	    /// refuses it; there is no 16-bit fallback for a gained export, because
261	    /// the gain would then meet a decode that already clipped.
262	    private func addAudioOutput() -> Bool {
263	        let output = Self.audioReadOutput(built, gained: audioGain != nil)
264	        guard reader.canAdd(output) else { return false }
265	        reader.add(output)
266	        audioOutput = output
267	        return true
268	    }

271	
272	    /// Starts the write. Main thread; `completion` is called exactly once, on
273	    /// the main thread, and may be called before this returns if the writer
274	    /// refuses to start at all.
275	    func start(completion: @escaping (Result<URL, any Error>) -> Void) {
276	        self.completion = completion
277	        // A cancel that arrived BEFORE this call is honoured here, before the
278	        // reader or the writer has started, rather than one sample later.
279	        lock.lock()
280	        let cancelledAlready = cancelRequested
281	        lock.unlock()
282	        guard !cancelledAlready else {
283	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
284	            return
285	        }
286	        if audioInput != nil, !addAudioOutput() {
287	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
288	                "The audio mix could not be read for export.")))
289	            return
290	        }
291	        guard writer.startWriting() else {
292	            report(.failure(writer.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
293	                "The file could not be opened for writing.")))
294	            return
295	        }
296	        guard reader.startReading() else {
297	            writer.cancelWriting()
298	            report(.failure(reader.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
299	                "The composition could not be read for export.")))
300	            return
301	        }
302	        // Zero, not `range.start`: the samples are rebased on the way in, so
303	        // the file's timeline is its own.
304	        writer.startSession(atSourceTime: .zero)
305	
306	        let group = DispatchGroup()
307	        if let input = videoInput, let output = videoOutput, let encodePump {
308	            encodePump.run(
309	                sink: ExportMP4PacketSink(input: input, format: encodePump.formatDescription),
310	                output: output, on: videoQueue, group: group,
311	                isStopping: { [weak self] in self?.isStopping ?? true },
312	                readFailure: { [weak self] in self?.readFailure },
313	                fail: { [weak self] error in self?.stopped(with: error) },
314	                advance: { [weak self] time in self?.advance(to: time) })
315	        } else if let input = videoInput, let output = videoOutput {
316	            pump(
317	                input, from: output, on: videoQueue, group: group, tracksProgress: true,
318	                frames: frames)
319	        }
320	        if let input = audioInput, let output = audioOutput {
321	            // Audio drives the bar only when there is no picture to drive it,
322	            // and it is the only pump that can carry a gain.
323	            pump(
324	                input, from: output, on: audioQueue, group: group,
325	                tracksProgress: videoInput == nil, gain: audioGain, end: audioEnd)
326	        }
327	        if let input = chapterInput {
328	            pumpChapters(input, on: chapterQueue, group: group)
329	        }
330	        group.notify(queue: .main) { [weak self] in self?.allInputsFinished() }
331	    }

333	    /// Stops as soon as the pumps notice — within one sample. Safe from any
334	    /// thread and safe to call twice. It ONLY sets the flag: the reader and
335	    /// the writer are cancelled in `allInputsFinished`, after every pump has
336	    /// left its loop.
337	    ///
338	    /// **Cancelling the reader from here crashed the app** (road map 10
339	    /// §10.6, G3c). `reader.cancelReading()` on main while a pump was inside
340	    /// `copyNextSampleBuffer` tore the reader down under it: EXC_BREAKPOINT
341	    /// in `CMVideoFormatDescriptionMatchesImageBuffer` on the video queue, in
342	    /// 12 of 30 mid-export cancels of a 4K graphic project — the sheet's and
343	    /// the queue's Cancel path — and 16 of 40 exports stopped by a failing
344	    /// graphic. The cost is that a pump blocked on a slow read finishes that
345	    /// one sample before it stops — and a `copyNextSampleBuffer` that never
346	    /// returns (a pump starved because the other stopped reading) can no
347	    /// longer be woken by a cancel, so the completion would never fire; not
348	    /// seen in 70 runs, and accepted (spec §11 G-17). A cancel before `start` is refused there;
349	    /// `cancelReading()` before `startReading()` would raise.
350	    func cancel() {
351	        lock.lock()
352	        cancelRequested = true
353	        lock.unlock()
354	    }
355	
356	    /// 0…1, from the last sample appended. `AVAssetWriter` has no progress of
357	    /// its own, so this is it.
358	    var progress: Double {
359	        lock.lock()
360	        defer { lock.unlock() }
361	        return progressValue
362	    }
363	
364	    // MARK: - The pumps
365	
366	    /// Moves one output's samples into one input until the output runs dry,
367	    /// the write fails, or the export is cancelled.
368	    ///
369	    /// `requestMediaDataWhenReady` re-enters this block whenever the encoder
370	    /// has room, so the "have I already finished?" flag lives outside it and
371	    /// is only ever touched on `queue`, which is serial.
372	    ///
373	    /// `gain` is nil for every pump but the audio one, and nil for the audio
374	    /// one too unless the export asked to be normalised — which is what
375	    /// keeps an ordinary export on exactly the samples it had before.
376	    /// `frames` is non-nil only for the video pump of a row `frameForm`
377	    /// names: each frame is then converted by it (`ExportFrames`).
378	    private func pump(
379	        _ input: AVAssetWriterInput, from output: AVAssetReaderOutput, on queue: DispatchQueue,
380	        group: DispatchGroup, tracksProgress: Bool, gain: ExportAudioGain? = nil,
381	        frames: ExportFrames? = nil, end: ExportAudioEnd? = nil
382	    ) {
383	        group.enter()
384	        var finished = false
385	        let stop: () -> Void = {
386	            guard !finished else { return }
387	            finished = true
388	            input.markAsFinished()
389	            group.leave()
390	        }
391	        input.requestMediaDataWhenReady(on: queue) { [weak self] in
392	            guard let self = self else { return }
393	            while input.isReadyForMoreMediaData {
394	                guard !finished else { return }
395	                guard !self.isStopping else {
396	                    stop()
397	                    return
398	                }
399	                guard let decoded = end?.isPadding == true ? nil : output.copyNextSampleBuffer()
400	                else {
401	                    // Dry for one of three reasons: the range is written, the
402	                    // read was cancelled (which `allInputsFinished` reports),
403	                    // or the read failed — and only the last is ours to name.
404	                    if self.reader.status == .failed {
405	                        self.stopped(
406	                            with: self.reader.error
407	                                ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
408	                                    "The composition could not be read to the end."))
409	                    } else if let end = end, !self.isStopping {
410	                        // Silence up to the range's end, while the input has room (#337).
411	                        guard let padded = end.pad(input) else { return }
412	                        if !padded {
413	                            self.stopped(with: self.writer.error
414	                                ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
415	                        }
416	                    }
417	                    stop()
418	                    return
419	                }
420	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(decoded) - self.range.start
421	                // A sample that starts before the range does not belong to
422	                // this file. The reader clips to `timeRange`, so this is a
423	                // boundary frame, not a common case.
424	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
425	                // An empty buffer has nothing to gain and is not malformed:
426	                // it is skipped, as the old Int16 kernel passed it through.
427	                if gain != nil, CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(decoded) == 0 { continue }
428	                // The gain makes a NEW 16-bit buffer from the float one,
429	                // before `retimed`; with no gain the decode goes on as read.
430	                guard let sample = gain == nil ? decoded : gain?.apply(to: decoded) else {
431	                    self.stopped(
432	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
433	                            "The loudness gain could not be applied to a sample."))
434	                    stop()
435	                    return
436	                }
437	                // A `frameForm` row's frame, converted (spec §11 G-35, PR-3),
438	                // before `retimed`; any other goes on as read.
439	                guard let ready = frames == nil ? sample : frames?.convert(sample) else {
440	                    self.stopped(
441	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
442	                            frames?.failure ?? "A frame could not be prepared for the encoder."))
443	                    stop()
444	                    return
445	                }
446	                guard let rebased = Self.retimed(ready, by: self.range.start) else {
447	                    self.stopped(
448	                        with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
449	                            "A sample could not be re-timed for the file."))
450	                    stop()
451	                    return
452	                }
453	                // A buffer past the range's end is cut or dropped (#337).
454	                guard let fitted = end == nil ? rebased : end?.fit(rebased) else { continue }
455	                guard input.append(fitted) else {
456	                    self.stopped(
457	                        with: self.writer.error
458	                            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The file could not be written."))
459	                    stop()
460	                    return
461	                }
462	                if tracksProgress { self.advance(to: time) }
463	            }
464	        }
465	    }
466	
467	    // MARK: - Finishing
468	
469	    /// True once anything has asked the write to stop.
470	    var isStopping: Bool {
471	        lock.lock()
472	        defer { lock.unlock() }
473	        return cancelRequested || failure != nil
474	    }
475	
476	    /// Records the first failure; later ones are noise from the other pumps
477	    /// unwinding. The other pumps see it before their next sample, and the
478	    /// read is cancelled in `allInputsFinished` (`cancel`'s doc says why).
479	    private func stopped(with error: any Error) {
480	        lock.lock()
481	        if failure == nil { failure = error }
482	        lock.unlock()
483	    }
484	
485	    /// The reader's error once its read failed, else nil — the encoder pump's question
486	    /// at the end of its read, worded as `pump`'s.
487	    private var readFailure: (any Error)? {
488	        guard reader.status == .failed else { return nil }
489	        return reader.error
490	            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The composition could not be read to the end.")
491	    }
492	
493	    private func advance(to time: CMTime) {
494	        guard totalSeconds > 0 else { return }
495	        let fraction = CMTimeGetSeconds(time) / totalSeconds
496	        lock.lock()
497	        progressValue = min(max(fraction, progressValue), 1)
498	        lock.unlock()
499	    }
500	
501	    /// Main thread, once every input has marked itself finished — so no pump
502	    /// is inside `copyNextSampleBuffer`, and the reader can be cancelled.
503	    private func allInputsFinished() {
504	        lock.lock()
505	        let error = failure
506	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
507	        lock.unlock()
508	        if error != nil || cancelled { reader.cancelReading() }
509	        encodePump?.close()
510	        if let error = error {
511	            writer.cancelWriting()
512	            report(.failure(error))
513	            return
514	        }
515	        if cancelled {
516	            // `cancelWriting` deletes the part-written file itself, which is
517	            // the same outcome the progress sheet arranges for a cancel.
518	            writer.cancelWriting()
519	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
520	            return
521	        }
522	        writer.finishWriting { [weak self] in
523	            // AVFoundation calls this on a queue of its own.
524	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.writingFinished() }
525	        }
526	    }
527	
528	    private func writingFinished() {
529	        lock.lock()
530	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
531	        lock.unlock()
532	        // A cancel that lands while the container is being closed still means
533	        // "I do not want this file": the sheet removes the destination on a
534	        // cancelled result, and a file the user cancelled out of is not one to
535	        // hand back because the timing was unlucky.
536	        guard !cancelled else {
537	            report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled))
538	            return
539	        }
540	        guard writer.status == .completed else {
541	            report(
542	                .failure(
543	                    writer.error
544	                        ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The export stopped before it finished.")))
545	            return
546	        }
547	        // The `av01` brand AVAssetWriter leaves out (spec §11 CX-12 (4)).
548	        if encodePump != nil {
549	            do {
550	                try ExportAV1Track.brandFile(destination)
551	            } catch {
552	                report(.failure(error))
553	                return
554	            }
555	        }
556	        lock.lock()
557	        progressValue = 1
558	        lock.unlock()
559	        report(.success(destination))
560	    }
561	
562	    /// The one exit, main thread, at most once.
563	    private func report(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
564	        guard let completion = completion else { return }
565	        self.completion = nil
566	        completion(result)
567	    }
568	}

1	import AVFoundation

     4	/// The `av1_webm` row's pipeline (spec §11 CX-15): the composed movie read back exactly as
     5	/// `ExportWriter` reads it, its picture encoded by the same `ExportEncodePump` and its sound
     6	/// by `ExportOpusEncoder`, written into a WebM by the core (`ReelWebM`).
     7	///
     8	/// **A second `ExportPipeline`, and the exception to §7.8's one writer (CX-15 (2)).**
     9	/// `AVAssetWriter` writes no WebM, so this file is the WebM half of `ExportWriter` and
    10	/// nothing more: the same reader outputs (`ExportWriter.videoReadOutput` /
    11	/// `audioReadOutput`), each on a reader of its own (below), the same gain (`ExportAudioGain`), the same end of the sound
    12	/// (`ExportAudioEnd`, #337), the same chapters (`ExportChapter.partition`), the same size and
    13	/// rates (`encodedSize`, the pump). What is its own is the container: the core interleaves,
    14	/// clusters, cues and closes the file. **A composition with no audio track is a silent
    15	/// movie**, as in `ExportWriter.addAudio`: no audio output, encoder or queue, and the layout
    16	/// has no audio track.
    17	///
    18	/// **Two pumps.** The video pump is `ExportEncodePump` on `videoQueue` into an
    19	/// `ExportWebMPacketSink`. The audio pump reads, checks the time, applies the gain, cuts at
    20	/// the range (`end.fit`), encodes and adds, on `audioQueue`; once the read is dry it encodes
    21	/// the padding silence and the encoder's tail and cuts the surplus by DiscardPadding
    22	/// (CX-15 (5)). The sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), so a dropped
    23	/// straddling buffer or a hole in the stamps keeps later sound where it was. Neither waits
    24	/// on the file: the core queues what the interleave holds.
    25	///
    26	/// **One `AVAssetReader` per output (CX-15 (2), (6)).** Two outputs of ONE reader are
    27	/// coupled: an output nobody reads stalls the reader, so a pump that stopped could leave the
    28	/// other blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` for good, and `cancelReading()` cannot wake it —
    29	/// AVFoundation forbids it concurrently with a read, and it crashed (G-17). So the video
    30	/// composition output and the audio mix output each have their own reader over the same
    31	/// composition (measured: the same frames byte for byte and the same sound sample for
    32	/// sample, `webm_export_proof.py` R1), neither read waits on the other, and each pump, once it
    33	/// has left its loop on a stop, cancels its own reader on its own queue — no thread ever
    34	/// cancels another's (G-17's rule). A silent movie has the video reader alone.
    35	///
    36	/// **Cancellation, failure and progress** are `ExportWriter`'s: a flag both pumps read
    37	/// before each read, the first failure recorded once (`stopped(with:)`, logged), progress
    38	/// from the frames submitted. A cancelled or failed export drops the writer and removes the
    39	/// file; a finished one is closed by `ReelWebM.finish()` off the main thread and reported on
    40	/// main. `-RCDevWebMFault` (`ExportWebMDevFault`, dev tools only) puts a fault in either

   242	        }

   271	                }
   272	            }

   274	                try feed(try opus.encode(silence))
   275	            }

   278	            // target is cut whole packets first, then by the last one's DiscardPadding.

   152	        }

   154	        do {
   155	            webm = try ReelWebM(path: destination.path, layoutJSON: layoutJSON)
   156	        } catch {
   157	            // The core creates the file before it writes the header: remove what it left.
   158	            discard()
   159	            return report(.failure(Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   160	                "The WebM file could not be made: \(error.localizedDescription)")))
   161	        }
   162	        self.webm = webm
   163	        guard videoReader.startReading() else {
   164	            discard()
   165	            return report(.failure(videoReader.error ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   166	                "The composition could not be read for export.")))
   167	        }

   169	        if let audioReader, audioReader.status == .unknown, !audioReader.startReading() {

   173	                "The audio mix could not be read for export.")))
   174	        }

   177	            sink: ExportWebMPacketSink(webm: webm, fault: fault), output: videoOutput,
   178	            on: videoQueue, group: group, isStopping: { [weak self] in self?.isStopping ?? true },
   179	            readFailure: { [weak self] in self?.readFailure(of: self?.videoReader) },
   180	            fail: { [weak self] error in self?.stopped(with: error) },
   181	            advance: { [weak self] time in self?.advance(to: time) })
   182	        // The video reader's own cancel, on its queue after the pump's read loop (G-17).
   183	        group.enter()
   184	        videoQueue.async { [self] in
   185	            defer { group.leave() }
   186	            if isStopping { videoReader.cancelReading() }
   187	        }

   189	            group.enter()

   191	                defer { group.leave() }
   192	                pumpAudio(output, into: webm, through: opus)
   193	                // Its own reader, after its own last read (G-17).
   194	                if isStopping { audioReader.cancelReading() }

   200	    /// Sets the flag; both pumps see it before their next sample. Any thread, any time.
   201	    func cancel() {
   202	        lock.lock()
   203	        cancelRequested = true
   204	        lock.unlock()
   205	    }
   206	
   207	    var progress: Double {
   208	        lock.lock()
   209	        defer { lock.unlock() }
   210	        return progressValue
   211	    }
   212	
   213	    // MARK: - The audio pump
   214	
   215	    /// Reads the mix to its end, encodes it and adds each packet, holding the newest back so
   216	    /// the last one can carry the tail's DiscardPadding (CX-15 (5)), or stops at the flag
   217	    /// before a read.
   218	    ///
   219	    /// **Times are the stamps'.** Each buffer is placed at its rebased stamp
   220	    /// (`ExportAudioEnd.align`: silence for a gap, the covered head cut), so the stream the
   221	    /// encoder is fed is the timeline's sound frame for frame from the range's start, and
   222	    /// packet k's first frame is the one stamped k × 960 / 48 kHz — k × 20 ms, a whole tick of
   223	    /// WebM's 1 ms timecode scale — which is the time it is added at.
   224	    private func pumpAudio(
   225	        _ output: AVAssetReaderOutput, into webm: ReelWebM, through opus: ExportOpusEncoder
   226	    ) {
   227	        let gain = audioGain
   228	        var held: Data?
   229	        var added: Int64 = 0
   230	        let packetNs = Int64(ExportOpusEncoder.framesPerPacket) * 1_000_000_000 / 48_000
   231	        let add = { (packet: Data, padding: Int64) throws in
   232	            try webm.add(
   233	                track: ReelWebM.audio, ptsNs: added * packetNs, key: true,
   234	                discardPaddingNs: padding, data: packet)
   235	            added += 1
   236	        }
   237	        let feed = { (packets: [Data]) throws in
   238	            for packet in packets {
   239	                if let previous = held { try add(previous, 0) }
   240	                held = packet
   241	            }
   242	        }
   243	        var reads = 0
   244	        do {
   245	            while true {
   246	                guard !isStopping else { return }
   247	                reads += 1
   248	                try fault?.beforeAudioRead(reads)

   250	                    if let error = readFailure(of: audioReader) {
   251	                        stopped(with: error)
   252	                        return
   253	                    }
   254	                    break
   255	                }
   256	                let time = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(decoded) - range.start
   257	                guard time.isNumeric, time >= .zero else { continue }
   258	                if gain != nil, CMSampleBufferGetNumSamples(decoded) == 0 { continue }

   260	                    stopped(with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   261	                        "The loudness gain could not be applied to a sample."))
   262	                    return
   263	                }
   264	                let frame = CMTimeConvertScale(
   265	                    time, timescale: CMTimeScale(ExportAudioEnd.sampleRate),
   266	                    method: .roundHalfAwayFromZero
   267	                ).value
   268	                for placed in audioEnd.align(sample, at: Int(frame)) {
   269	                    guard let fitted = audioEnd.fit(placed) else { continue }
   270	                    try feed(try opus.encode(fitted))
   271	                }
   272	            }
   273	            for silence in audioEnd.padding() {
   274	                try feed(try opus.encode(silence))
   275	            }
   276	            var tail = (held.map { [$0] } ?? []) + (try opus.finish())
   277	            // The decoded length is packets × 960 − pre-skip; the surplus over #337's
   278	            // target is cut whole packets first, then by the last one's DiscardPadding.
   279	            var padding = (Int(added) + tail.count) * ExportOpusEncoder.framesPerPacket
   280	                - opus.preSkip - audioEnd.target
   281	            while padding >= ExportOpusEncoder.framesPerPacket, !tail.isEmpty {
   282	                tail.removeLast()
   283	                padding -= ExportOpusEncoder.framesPerPacket
   284	            }

   286	                stopped(with: Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   287	                    "The audio could not be encoded to its exact length."))
   288	                return
   289	            }
   290	            let paddingNs = (Int64(padding) * 1_000_000_000 + 24_000) / 48_000
   291	            for (index, packet) in tail.enumerated() {
   292	                try add(packet, index == tail.count - 1 ? paddingNs : 0)
   293	            }
   294	            try webm.endTrack(ReelWebM.audio)
   295	        } catch {
   296	            stopped(with: error)
   297	        }
   298	    }

   300	    // MARK: - Finishing
   301	
   302	    private var isStopping: Bool {
   303	        lock.lock()
   304	        defer { lock.unlock() }
   305	        return cancelRequested || failure != nil
   306	    }
   307	
   308	    private func stopped(with error: any Error) {
   309	        lock.lock()
   310	        let first = failure == nil
   311	        if first { failure = error }
   312	        lock.unlock()
   313	        // The unified log (not stdout or the proofs' log), so a stop names its cause.
   314	        let which = first ? "first" : "later"
   315	        let why = error.localizedDescription
   316	        Self.log.error(
   317	            "WebM export stopped (\(which, privacy: .public)): \(why, privacy: .public)")
   318	    }
   319	
   320	    private static let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.kgalligan.FrameJob", category: "export.webm")
   321	
   322	    private func readFailure(of reader: AVAssetReader?) -> (any Error)? {
   323	        guard let reader, reader.status == .failed else { return nil }
   324	        return reader.error
   325	            ?? Exporter.ExportError.failed("The composition could not be read to the end.")
   326	    }
   327	
   328	    private func advance(to time: CMTime) {
   329	        guard totalSeconds > 0 else { return }
   330	        let fraction = CMTimeGetSeconds(time) / totalSeconds
   331	        lock.lock()
   332	        progressValue = min(max(fraction, progressValue), 1)
   333	        lock.unlock()
   334	    }
   335	
   336	    /// Main thread, once both pumps have left (each reader already cancelled by its own
   337	    /// pump on a stop): the encoder closed, then the file finished off main or dropped and
   338	    /// removed.
   339	    private func allPumpsLeft() {
   340	        lock.lock()
   341	        let error = failure
   342	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
   343	        lock.unlock()
   344	        if fault != nil {
   345	            let shared = audioReader === videoReader ? " (one reader)" : ""
   346	            ExportWebMDevFault.log(
   347	                "readers: video \(videoReader.status.rawValue), audio "
   348	                    + (audioReader.map { "\($0.status.rawValue)" } ?? "none") + shared)
   349	        }
   350	        pump.close()
   351	        if let error { return finishFailed(error) }
   352	        if cancelled { return finishFailed(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled) }
   353	        guard let webm else { return finishFailed(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled) }
   354	        videoQueue.async { [weak self] in
   355	            let closed: (any Error)?
   356	            do {
   357	                try webm.finish()
   358	                closed = nil
   359	            } catch {
   360	                closed = Exporter.ExportError.failed(
   361	                    "The WebM file could not be finished: \(error.localizedDescription)")
   362	            }
   363	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.fileClosed(closed) }
   364	        }
   365	    }
   366	
   367	    private func fileClosed(_ error: (any Error)?) {
   368	        lock.lock()
   369	        let cancelled = cancelRequested
   370	        lock.unlock()
   371	        if let error { return finishFailed(error) }
   372	        // A cancel while the file was being closed still means "I do not want this file".
   373	        if cancelled { return finishFailed(Exporter.ExportError.cancelled) }

   375	        progressValue = 1
   376	        lock.unlock()
   377	        report(.success(destination))
   378	    }

   380	    private func finishFailed(_ error: any Error) {
   381	        discard()
   382	        report(.failure(error))
   383	    }

   386	    private func discard() {
   387	        webm = nil
   388	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: destination)
   389	    }
   390	
   391	    /// The one exit, main thread, at most once.
   392	    private func report(_ result: Result<URL, any Error>) {
   393	        guard let completion else { return }
   394	        self.completion = nil
   395	        completion(result)
   396	    }

  playhead"): the front track if the clip fits there, else a new track
  above everything. So no track, or a playhead over a clip, never disables
  the item; it validates on the document's graphics store alone.
  (b) **The name is the file's stem made a module name, then made free**:
  lowercased, every run of anything but `a-z0-9` one `-`, trimmed, at most
  63 (`graphic` when nothing is left) — `My Counter (v2).js` is
  `my-counter-v2` — then `GraphicStore.uniqueModuleName`: the name when
  the folder holds no module of it, else `-2`, `-3`, …, so an insert never
  overwrites a module another clip draws. Duplicate as New Graphic…'s
  suggestion uses the same rule.
  (c) **A module that does not compile stays on disk and places nothing**:
  the person reads "graphics/<name>.js was written but does not compile:
  <the first diagnostic> (line N)" in a sheet, and can fix the file where

- **G-17 — An export's Cancel only sets flags; a reader is cancelled only
  by the loop that reads it, and a read that never returns is not woken —
  accepted** (issues #73, #74, 2026-09-29). `ExportWriter.cancel()` and
  `Exporter.cancel()` set flags and nothing else. The measurement's loop
  (`Exporter.measureLoudness`) sees the flag between samples and cancels
  its own reader; the writer's reader and writer are cancelled in
  `allInputsFinished`, after every pump has left its loop. Why:
  `cancelReading()` from main while a pump was inside
  `copyNextSampleBuffer` crashed 12 of 30 mid-export cancels (road map 10
  §10.6 G3c, #38). A cross-thread watchdog that cancels a stuck reader is
  that same mechanism again, and abandoning the completion instead would
  leave a live reader and writer on the destination. The risk accepted: a
  read that never returns (a pump starved because the other stopped
  reading, or a volume that stops answering) keeps its export alive — the
  sheet or the queue's job never completes and the queue stalls behind it,
  and an MCP `export` holds the server until its one-hour ceiling. Not seen
  in 70 runs (G3c) nor in issue batch B1's M1 runs
  (`tools/proof/export_cancel_proof.py`). Revisit only if one is observed.

  crosses a frame grid; a graphic clip with no description is tolerated**
  (issue #72, 2026-09-29).
  (a) **`add_transition`'s handle form moves `in` back by the head
  extension** through `graphic_advanced`, its fourth writer. G-9·a stands —
  no head bound — so where `in` is less than the extension it saturates at
  0 and the graphic's first frame lands on the clip's new first frame:
  `trim_start`'s answer at 0, and the one step 9 gives a text reveal.
  (b) **`graphic.in` is not a source position in D7-3's sense**: the

  frame)`). So every re-snap through `frame_grid.rs` (`set_canvas` fps,
  both paste paths, `unnest`) snaps `in` to the nearest frame, ≥ 0, and a
  set `length` to the nearest frame with `set_graphic`'s one-frame floor. A
  null length stays null.

  no `graphic`.** The recipe answers `missing`, and the app draws the slate
  it draws for missing media. `set_graphic` answers `clip N is not a
  graphic clip`, so the clip is deleted rather than repaired. Refusing
  would make a whole document unreadable over a clip that holds nothing,
  which is `validate`'s canvas posture (model_query.rs:205-208).

  (a) **`format: "svg"` refuses a non-null `path`, `background` or

| Rate | Faster | Balanced | Smaller file |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | Low | 91.611 (40), 92.235 (38), **92.828 (36)** | **93.351 (36)** | **93.316 (36)** |
     | Medium | 95.165 (28), **95.471 (26)** | 95.203 (30), **95.617 (28)** | 95.103 (30), **95.498 (28)** |
     | Format default | 95.982 (24), **96.193 (22)** | 96.048 (26), **96.487 (24)** | 95.924 (26), **96.377 (24)** |
     | High | 96.278 (22), **96.447 (20)** | **96.505 (24)** | **96.385 (24)** |
     | Maximum | 97.282 (14), **97.376 (12)**, 97.296 (10), 97.325 (8), 97.298 (6), 97.266 (4) | **97.568 (16)** | **97.492 (16)** |

     So the table became Low 36 / 36 / 36, Medium 26 / 28 / 28, Format default 22 / 24 / 24,
     High 20 / 24 / 24 and Maximum 12 / 16 / 16. Faster's Medium, which the promo half bound
     in CX-13 (28), is now bound by the owner clip at 10 bits (26). **Faster at Maximum
     reached no CRF:** from 12 down the cap binds (0.93–1.03 × it) and the VMAF stays
     0.06–0.17 under `hevc_10bit`'s 97.435. **Accepted (owner, 2026-10-28, "Best CRF,
     accept 0.06"):** the cell is 12, the best measured, at 97.376 — 0.059 under
     `hevc_10bit`'s 97.435 and still 0.53 above C1's 8-bit `hevc` comparator (96.85) —
     because below CRF 12 the cap binds and a lower CRF gains nothing.

- **CX-15 — C3: `av1_webm`, the core's WebM writer and Opus** (default, recorded in C3 before
  its code; amends CX-6, CX-7, CX-12 (1), CX-14 (2), HD-5 and HD-14 (c)):
  1. **The row.** `av1_webm` is "AV1 (WebM)", directly after `av1`: container `webm`
     (`org.webmproject.webm`), codec `av1`, video, no alpha, `size` and `fps` null,
     `avf_preset` `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough`, `"hdr": true`, `writer` `svt_av1` and
     `av1`'s `encoder_speeds`. It is even-sized and one of HD-5's HDR rows. It shares `av1`'s
     speeds, CX-13's cap and CRF table, and CX-14's I010, CICP and PQ HDR10, all through the
     same `SVTAV1Encoder`. `optimize_for_network` defaults to false and has no effect on this
     row, as it has none on WAV.
  2. **The writer is a second `ExportPipeline`, an exception to §7.8's one-writer argument.**
     `Exporter.pipeline` chooses `ExportWebMWriter` for the `webm` container. It reads through
     the same reader outputs as `ExportWriter` and the same `ExportEncodePump`, and uses the
     same `ExportAudioGain`, `ExportAudioEnd`, `ExportChapter.partition`,
     `encodedSize`/`fillsTheBox` and bitrate resolution, so chapters, rates, size, range and
     #337 are one decision each. **A composition with no audio track is a silent movie, as in
     `ExportWriter.addAudio`:** the layout has no `audio`, and no audio reader output, Opus
     encoder or audio queue is made. **One `AVAssetReader` per output** (fix pass 1): the
     video composition output on a reader of its own, the audio mix output on another, both
     over the same composition and range (a silent movie has the video reader alone). WHY:
     two outputs of one reader are coupled — an output nobody reads stalls the reader — so
     on a shared reader a stop on one pump could leave the other blocked in
     `copyNextSampleBuffer` for good (G-17's starvation, seen once in C3), and
     `cancelReading()` cannot wake it: AVFoundation's header forbids calling it concurrently
     with a read, and G-17 measured it crashing. With a reader each, neither read waits on
     the other; the other pump sees a recorded stop at its next check and leaves, and each
     pump, after its own last read, cancels its own reader on its own queue — G-17's rule,
     no thread cancelling another's reader. Two readers read what one did: the same 150
     frames byte for byte (I010 of the first, middle and last too) and the same 240,000
     frames of sound (`webm_export_proof.py` R1, measured before the change).
  3. **The layout.**
     - The header is EBML with DocType `webm`, DocTypeVersion 4 and DocTypeReadVersion 2. The
       Segment size is written as 8 bytes and patched at finish. A Void reserved after the
       Segment header is overwritten at finish by a SeekHead (Info, Tracks, Chapters when
       present, Cues).
     - Info has TimestampScale 1,000,000, Duration = duration_ns / 1e6, and MuxingApp and
       WritingApp "Frame Job".
     - Track 1 (UID 1) carries `V_AV1` with the `av1C` record as CodecPrivate, DefaultDuration
       round(1e9 · den / num) ns, PixelWidth and PixelHeight, and Colour (the sequence
       header's CICP, Range 1, BitsPerChannel 10). On PQ alone, Colour also carries MaxCLL,
       MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata decoded from `OutputTransform`'s two blobs.
     - Track 2 (UID 2), when the layout has audio, carries `A_OPUS` with OpusHead version 1 as
       CodecPrivate (channels, pre-skip, 48,000, gain 0, mapping family 0), CodecDelay
       round(pre_skip · 1e9 / 48,000) ns, SeekPreRoll 80,000,000 ns, and Audio at 48,000.0 Hz
       with its channel count.
     - Chapters are one EditionEntry (UID 1) holding one ChapterAtom per chapter (UID i + 1,
       start, end), each with a ChapterDisplay (ChapString, ChapLanguage `und`).
     - Block times are round-half-up(pts_ns / 1e6) ms. SimpleBlocks are written in
       nondecreasing time, video first among equal times, with the key flag on video keys and
       on every audio block. A packet with a DiscardPadding above 0 is written as a BlockGroup
       with DiscardPadding.
     - A new Cluster starts before each video key block, and before any block whose relative
       time would pass 32,767 ms. The Cues hold one CuePoint per key-started Cluster
       (CueTime, track 1, CueClusterPosition from the Segment's data) and are written at
       finish.
  4. **Interleave.** The core buffers each track the layout declares. It writes the earliest
     head only while every declared track that has not ended has a head, and `end_track`
     releases that constraint; a layout with one track writes each packet as it arrives. The
     memory bound accepted is the whole Opus track at worst, about 1.4 MB a minute at
     192 kb/s. Back-pressure on the audio pump is not used, because a stalled output starves
     the shared reader (G-17's note).
  5. **Opus.** AudioToolbox (CX-7) at 48 kHz stereo in 20 ms packets. The default is
     192 kb/s, the AAC rows' own number, so the more efficient codec matches or beats AAC at
     the same rate. `audio_bitrate` and the Quality tiers pass through, snapped to the
     converter's `applicableEncodeBitRates`. The pre-skip is `primeInfo.leadingFrames`.
     **The tail:** the encoder's `finish()` feeds pre-skip frames of silence before the end
     of stream, so that packets × 960 ≥ pre-skip + `ExportAudioEnd.target` holds by
     construction. The writer computes padding = packets × 960 − pre-skip − target frames,
     drops whole trailing packets while the padding is 960 or more, and fails the export
     ("The audio could not be encoded to its exact length.") if it is below 0. The last
     packet carries the padding (in ns) as DiscardPadding, so the decoded length is #337's
     exactly. **The sound is placed at its stamps** (fix pass 1): each buffer's rebased
     stamp decides where it goes (`ExportAudioEnd.align`) — zeros for a gap before it (a
     straddling buffer dropped at the range's start, a hole in the stamps), the frames
     already covered cut from its head — so packet k's first frame is the one stamped
     k × 20 ms, the time it is written at. The encoder's FIFO counts a buffer's frames from
     its bytes; bytes that are not whole 16-bit stereo frames fail the export in a sentence.
  6. **Risks accepted:** a second writer to keep in step with `ExportWriter`; no player's HDR
     rendering of WebM was measured; CX-10 holds (no re-import on an M1 or M2); and the
     composition decoded by two readers, not one (the audio reader reads only the audio
     tracks, so the extra cost is their decode). **G-17's starvation is closed for WebM**
     by (2)'s per-output readers: an audio-pump failure, a video-sink failure and a cancel
     while the audio read is held each end within 10 s with no file and both readers
     cancelled by their own pumps (`webm_export_proof.py` F1–F3, `-RCDevWebMFault`); a
     shared reader is named every time only by the readers' log line, F1–F3's timings alone
     catching it only through G-17's crash. It stays accepted on `ExportWriter`'s shared
     reader (G-17), whose same fix is filed as #378.

     (`org.webmproject.webm`), codec `av1`, video, no alpha, `size` and `fps` null,
     `avf_preset` `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough`, `"hdr": true`, `writer` `svt_av1` and
     `av1`'s `encoder_speeds`. It is even-sized and one of HD-5's HDR rows. It shares `av1`'s
     speeds, CX-13's cap and CRF table, and CX-14's I010, CICP and PQ HDR10, all through the
     same `SVTAV1Encoder`. `optimize_for_network` defaults to false and has no effect on this
     row, as it has none on WAV.
  2. **The writer is a second `ExportPipeline`, an exception to §7.8's one-writer argument.**
     `Exporter.pipeline` chooses `ExportWebMWriter` for the `webm` container. It reads through
     the same reader outputs as `ExportWriter` and the same `ExportEncodePump`, and uses the
     same `ExportAudioGain`, `ExportAudioEnd`, `ExportChapter.partition`,
     `encodedSize`/`fillsTheBox` and bitrate resolution, so chapters, rates, size, range and
     #337 are one decision each. **A composition with no audio track is a silent movie, as in
     `ExportWriter.addAudio`:** the layout has no `audio`, and no audio reader output, Opus
     encoder or audio queue is made. **One `AVAssetReader` per output** (fix pass 1): the
     video composition output on a reader of its own, the audio mix output on another, both
     over the same composition and range (a silent movie has the video reader alone). WHY:
     two outputs of one reader are coupled — an output nobody reads stalls the reader — so
     on a shared reader a stop on one pump could leave the other blocked in
     `copyNextSampleBuffer` for good (G-17's starvation, seen once in C3), and
     `cancelReading()` cannot wake it: AVFoundation's header forbids calling it concurrently
     with a read, and G-17 measured it crashing. With a reader each, neither read waits on
     the other; the other pump sees a recorded stop at its next check and leaves, and each
     pump, after its own last read, cancels its own reader on its own queue — G-17's rule,
     no thread cancelling another's reader. Two readers read what one did: the same 150
     frames byte for byte (I010 of the first, middle and last too) and the same 240,000
     frames of sound (`webm_export_proof.py` R1, measured before the change).
  3. **The layout.**
     - The header is EBML with DocType `webm`, DocTypeVersion 4 and DocTypeReadVersion 2. The
       Segment size is written as 8 bytes and patched at finish. A Void reserved after the
       Segment header is overwritten at finish by a SeekHead (Info, Tracks, Chapters when
       present, Cues).
     - Info has TimestampScale 1,000,000, Duration = duration_ns / 1e6, and MuxingApp and
       WritingApp "Frame Job".
     - Track 1 (UID 1) carries `V_AV1` with the `av1C` record as CodecPrivate, DefaultDuration
       round(1e9 · den / num) ns, PixelWidth and PixelHeight, and Colour (the sequence
       header's CICP, Range 1, BitsPerChannel 10). On PQ alone, Colour also carries MaxCLL,
       MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata decoded from `OutputTransform`'s two blobs.
     - Track 2 (UID 2), when the layout has audio, carries `A_OPUS` with OpusHead version 1 as
       CodecPrivate (channels, pre-skip, 48,000, gain 0, mapping family 0), CodecDelay
       round(pre_skip · 1e9 / 48,000) ns, SeekPreRoll 80,000,000 ns, and Audio at 48,000.0 Hz
       with its channel count.
     - Chapters are one EditionEntry (UID 1) holding one ChapterAtom per chapter (UID i + 1,
       start, end), each with a ChapterDisplay (ChapString, ChapLanguage `und`).
     - Block times are round-half-up(pts_ns / 1e6) ms. SimpleBlocks are written in
       nondecreasing time, video first among equal times, with the key flag on video keys and
       on every audio block. A packet with a DiscardPadding above 0 is written as a BlockGroup
       with DiscardPadding.
     - A new Cluster starts before each video key block, and before any block whose relative
       time would pass 32,767 ms. The Cues hold one CuePoint per key-started Cluster
       (CueTime, track 1, CueClusterPosition from the Segment's data) and are written at
       finish.
  4. **Interleave.** The core buffers each track the layout declares. It writes the earliest
     head only while every declared track that has not ended has a head, and `end_track`
     releases that constraint; a layout with one track writes each packet as it arrives. The
     memory bound accepted is the whole Opus track at worst, about 1.4 MB a minute at
     192 kb/s. Back-pressure on the audio pump is not used, because a stalled output starves
     the shared reader (G-17's note).
  5. **Opus.** AudioToolbox (CX-7) at 48 kHz stereo in 20 ms packets. The default is
     192 kb/s, the AAC rows' own number, so the more efficient codec matches or beats AAC at
     the same rate. `audio_bitrate` and the Quality tiers pass through, snapped to the
     converter's `applicableEncodeBitRates`. The pre-skip is `primeInfo.leadingFrames`.
     **The tail:** the encoder's `finish()` feeds pre-skip frames of silence before the end
     of stream, so that packets × 960 ≥ pre-skip + `ExportAudioEnd.target` holds by
     construction. The writer computes padding = packets × 960 − pre-skip − target frames,
     drops whole trailing packets while the padding is 960 or more, and fails the export
     ("The audio could not be encoded to its exact length.") if it is below 0. The last
     packet carries the padding (in ns) as DiscardPadding, so the decoded length is #337's
     exactly. **The sound is placed at its stamps** (fix pass 1): each buffer's rebased
     stamp decides where it goes (`ExportAudioEnd.align`) — zeros for a gap before it (a
     straddling buffer dropped at the range's start, a hole in the stamps), the frames
     already covered cut from its head — so packet k's first frame is the one stamped
     k × 20 ms, the time it is written at. The encoder's FIFO counts a buffer's frames from
     its bytes; bytes that are not whole 16-bit stereo frames fail the export in a sentence.
  6. **Risks accepted:** a second writer to keep in step with `ExportWriter`; no player's HDR
     rendering of WebM was measured; CX-10 holds (no re-import on an M1 or M2); and the
     composition decoded by two readers, not one (the audio reader reads only the audio
     tracks, so the extra cost is their decode). **G-17's starvation is closed for WebM**

     cancelled by their own pumps (`webm_export_proof.py` F1–F3, `-RCDevWebMFault`); a

     catching it only through G-17's crash. It stays accepted on `ExportWriter`'s shared
     reader (G-17), whose same fix is filed as #378.

  playback, export and the ramp renderer, and it keeps passes FIFO. The two
  app mutants that take away one guard each survive by design, and their
  Release W1 times are the evidence: `unbounded` (width 64, off the pool)
  1.61 s, and `app-inline` (width 2, on the pool) 1.37 s, with a sample
  after P1 showing 2 cooperative threads in `copyNextSampleBuffer`. The
  scored mutants are `no-lane`, which takes away both and restores the old
  path (W1 FAIL on Release, S0 again 12 cooperative threads in
  `copyNextSampleBuffer`), and the probe's `wide` (L1, guard 2) and
  `inline` (L4, guard 1). With the lane on Release, W1's render landed
  1.37 s after its edit and W2 found all 60 of P1's cache markers 4.7 s
  after W1. Two is a concurrency bound, not a memory limit. Off the lane:
  thumbnails (`AVAssetImageGenerator`), the head checks
  (`peaksAreCurrent`, `syncFeaturesAreCurrent`, `speechIsCurrent`) and
  `pass.isCurrent()`, which run before a pass reaches the lane so a current
  cache never queues, and every other reader in the app (transcription's
  extract, the reverse renderer, export's loudness, the rate copy, the
  decoders, colour detection, sync analysis), which this change does not
  move. A pass's order (thumbnails, peaks, sync, speech, `retryPeaks`) is
  unchanged. W1 and W2 are `release_only` (V-4): they bound decode work in
  wall seconds, and a Debug decode runs about 17× slower (≈ 17.5 s for one
  250 s pass). **Risk accepted:** with many imports, later files' waveforms
  and sync and speech caches arrive later, two at a time in import order; a
  document closed while its passes wait still decodes them when their turn
  comes, as a running pass already did; and on a host whose cooperative
  pool is two threads or fewer, guard 2 alone would not hold, so there
  guard 1 is the only one.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Road map "codec-export" C3 — the `av1_webm` row: AV1 in WebM through the bundled
SVT-AV1, written by the core's own WebM writer (`rc_webm_*`), with Opus sound from
AudioToolbox (spec §11 CX-6, CX-7, CX-15).

    python3 tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH]
    python3 tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py --probe          # the P and A rows alone, no app
    python3 tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py --mutant NAME

Launches its own instances of the chosen app (`proof_app.py`: `--app`, else
`RC_PROOF_APP`, else Debug; a build older than its inputs is refused) on scratch
sockets, works under `tools/proof/work/webm-export/`, closes every project it opens
with `discard: true` and stops each instance by its own PID. It reuses
`av1_export_proof.py`'s helpers by import (its instance, documents, exports, ffprobe
readers and sheet reading). ffprobe and ffmpeg (Homebrew, with libdav1d and Opus) only
READ the files.

"A1's project" is `av1_export_proof.py`'s: AV.mov (640 × 360, 30 fps, 5 s) under a
two-second text clip; here it also carries two chapter markers, "Intro" at 0 s and
"Body" at 2.5 s. Each W row is ffprobe/ffmpeg over it exported as `av1_webm` unless it
says otherwise. Rows (`<ID> ok|FAIL — <detail>`, then `scores: n/m`; exit 0 iff all
passed):

* Z1 — every instance's log is silent (no `Frame Job: `, `Svt[` or `SVT-AV1: ` line).
* W1 — done; format `matroska,webm`; video `av1` Main `yuv420p10le` 640 × 360; audio
  `opus` 48 kHz stereo; the format's duration 5.0 s ± one frame.
* W2 — `ffmpeg -v error` decodes the file with no line; 150 video frames; exactly
  240,000 audio samples (the s16le stereo byte count / 4): #337's length through
  CodecDelay and DiscardPadding; and the first audio packet at −CodecDelay (ffprobe's
  `initial_padding`, the pre-skip, above 0 and the packet at −padding / 48 kHz in whole
  ms). The last because ffmpeg trims OpusHead's pre-skip whatever CodecDelay says, so the
  count alone does not see a CodecDelay of 0 (measured, C3).
* W3 — A5's key rule on the WebM's video blocks, their key flags read from the file by
  the walk (ffprobe's and `trace_headers`' flags for AV1 in Matroska are ffmpeg's AV1
  parser's, from the bitstream, so they cannot see the container's flag): the first a
  key, every key 2 s or less from the next, fewer keys than blocks, each block's key flag
  the bitstream's shown KEY_FRAME both ways, no hidden intra frame.
* W4 — a Python EBML walk of the file: the Segment's size is the file's length less
  the Segment's header; the SeekHead's entries (Info, Tracks, Chapters, Cues) each
  resolve to that element; every video key block starts a Cluster; the Cues hold one
  CuePoint per key-started Cluster, each at its Cluster's position and time.
* W5 — `ffprobe -show_chapters`: "Intro" 0.0–2.5 s and "Body" 2.5–5.0 s.
* W6 — the 1 s – 3 s in/out export: 60 frames, 96,000 samples, and the chapters
  clamped and rebased: "Intro" 0.0–1.5 s, "Body" 1.5–2.0 s.
* W7 — `size: [640, 480]` is 640 × 480 with the picture letterboxed (A8's rule).
* W8 — A1's project made HLG, exported at the default, `pq` and `sdr`: the answer's
  dynamic range; ffprobe's `yuv420p10le` / Main and its colour tags; the sequence
  headers' CICP (9/18/9, 9/16/9, 1/1/1, video range); the walk's Colour (the same
  CICP, Range 1, BitsPerChannel 10, and on PQ alone MasteringMetadata and MaxCLL 1000 /
  MaxFALL 0); on PQ the stream's mastering-display side data at HD-5's values (P3-D65,
  0.005–1,000 cd/m²), on the others no HDR side data. The light level is read from the
  walk alone: ffmpeg's Matroska demuxer exports a content-light-level side data only
  when MaxCLL and MaxFALL are both non-zero, and HD-5's MaxFALL is 0 (measured, C3).
* W9 — A6's cancel on a 24-clip 1080p project exported as `av1_webm`: cancelled
  within 10 s while encoding, and no file at the path.
* W10 — the default rate's audio bytes are more than 1.25 × those of an
  `audio_bitrate: 64000` export.
* W11 — with `loudness_lufs: -16`, ffmpeg ebur128's integrated loudness is −16 ± 1 LU.
* W12 — `import_media` of W1's file: on an M1 or M2, refused in
  `codec_import_proof.av1_sentence`'s words; on an M3 or later, a 5.0 s 640 × 360
  media with audio.
* W13 — a project holding only a 5 s text clip (no media, so no audio track) exported
  as `av1_webm`: done; exactly one stream, `av1` 640 × 360; `ffmpeg -v error` decodes
  150 frames with no line; the walk finds one TrackEntry.
* S4 — the export sheet pinned to `{"preset_id":"av1_webm"}` reads Format
  "AV1 (WebM)" and the footnote "AV1 · WEBM · Balanced".
* R1 — the measurement behind one reader per output (fix pass 1, CX-15 (2)): the probe
  `webm_readers_probe.swift` (no app; the tree's export shaders as its `default.metallib`)
  reads A1's project through `ExportWriter`'s two outputs on one reader and on two readers,
  each on a thread of its own, from builds of their own: 150 frames each, every frame's
  64RGBAHalf bytes equal, the I010 of frames 0, 75 and 149 byte-equal, and 240,000 frames of
  16-bit sound equal sample for sample.
* F1–F3 — G-17's windows closed on the WebM path: W9's 24-clip 1080p project exported as
  `av1_webm` on an instance launched with `-RCDevWebMFault` (`ExportWebMDevFault`): F1
  `audio@40` (the audio pump fails at its 40th read), F2 `video@30` (the video sink fails at
  its 30th packet), F3 `audio-hold@40` (the audio pump held 3 s at its 40th read, before the
  read, and `cancel_export` sent when the hold's log line appears). Each ends — F1 and F2
  `failed` naming the dev fault, F3 `cancelled` — within 10 s of the fault's log line (F3: of
  the cancel), with no file at the path, and the writer's `framejob webm dev readers:` line
  reads exactly `video 4, audio 4`: both readers cancelled (status 4) by their own pumps,
  and two readers (the line adds ` (one reader)` when the outputs share one).
* P1–P5, A1–A5 — the probe `webm_audio_probe.swift` (fix pass 1), compiled AS
  `main.swift` over `app/Sources` on `swift_build.py`'s line, no app: P1–P5 the Opus
  encoder's FIFO fed by the buffer's BYTES (a short last buffer, a buffer cut by `fit`, bytes
  that outrun or fall short of the sample count, and 402 bytes refused in a sentence);
  A1–A5 `ExportAudioEnd.align`, the sound placed at its stamps (zeros for a gap, the covered
  head cut, a buffer covered whole dropped, no gap untouched, the zeros stopped at the
  target). A probe that will not build is a scored FAIL of every P and A row.

Mutants (`--mutant NAME`, a tree copy built as Debug with the named anchor replaced;
exit 1 and `MUTANT CAUGHT` when exactly the named rows fail — `cargo-<file>` is that
cargo test file run in the copy):

  codec-delay-zero     the TrackEntry's CodecDelay written 0: W2, cargo. Not E38 or E39
                       (measured, C3): `export_offset_proof.py` places clicks by sample in
                       the decoded stream, and ffmpeg trims OpusHead's pre-skip whatever
                       CodecDelay says, so only the packets' times (W2) move
  no-discard-padding   the tail packet's DiscardPadding never sent: W2, W6
  clusters-by-time     Clusters every 1.5 s instead of at video keys: W4, cargo
  no-cues              no Cues written: W4
  colour-unwritten     no Colour element: W8, cargo
  chapters-unclamped   a chapter before the range not pinned to its start: W6
  all-key              every video block flagged key: W3
  gain-skipped         the loudness gain never kept: W11
  opus-length-exact    the encoder's old check, bytes = samples × 4, put back: P3, P4
                       (a probe mutant: the copy is `app/Sources` alone, no app built)
  gap-unfilled         `align` never fills a gap: A1, A5 (a probe mutant)
  head-uncut           `align` cuts a covered head from the buffer's tail: A2 (a probe mutant)
  shared-reader        the audio output put on the video's reader again: the F rows (a
                       fault mutant: the copy's app built, the F rows alone run)
  audio-cancel-dropped the audio pump's own `cancelReading` on a stop dropped: F1–F3 (a
                       fault mutant)

An instrument that cannot run is a FAIL, never an exit.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import av1_export_proof as av1  # noqa: E402
import bounded  # noqa: E402
import mcp  # noqa: E402
import proof_app  # noqa: E402
from codec_import_proof import av1_sentence  # noqa: E402

WORK = HERE / "work" / "webm-export"
av1.WORK = WORK            # the reused Instance and mutant builder work here
SEC = av1.SEC
FRAMES = 150
SAMPLES = 240_000          # 5 s at 48 kHz
CANCEL_BOUND = 10.0

  media with audio.

  each on a thread of its own, from builds of their own: 150 frames each, every frame's

  16-bit sound equal sample for sample.

def row_fault(ident, app, logs):
    spec, want = FAULTS[ident]
    instance = av1.Instance(f"fault-{ident.lower()}", app,
                            arguments=["-RCDevWebMFault", spec])

    marker = "is held" if ident == "F3" else "framejob webm dev fault:"

    def log_lines():
        try:
            return instance.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return []
    try:
        if instance.client is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the app did not listen ({instance.log})")
        doc = long_doc(instance, ident.lower())
        job = doc.client.call_with("export", {"project": doc.path, "path": str(path),
                                              "preset": "av1_webm"})["export_id"]
        deadline, fired = time.monotonic() + 300, None
        status = {}
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if any(marker in line for line in log_lines()):
                fired = time.monotonic()
                break
            status = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if status.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        if fired is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"the fault never fired: {status}")
        if ident == "F3":
            doc.client.call("cancel_export", export_id=job)
        final = {}
        while time.monotonic() - fired < 120:
            final = doc.client.call("export_status", export_id=job)
            if final.get("status") in ("done", "failed", "cancelled"):
                break
            time.sleep(0.05)
        took = time.monotonic() - fired
        time.sleep(0.5)    # the readers' line follows the pumps, on main
        readers = [line.split("readers: ", 1)[1] for line in log_lines() if "readers: " in line]
        exists = path.exists()
        named = want == "cancelled" or "dev fault" in json.dumps(final)
        ok = (final.get("status") == want and named and took <= FAULT_BOUND and not exists
              and readers == ["video 4, audio 4"])
        detail = (f"{spec}: status {final.get('status')!r} (want {want!r}) {took:.2f} s after "
                  f"the {'cancel' if ident == 'F3' else 'fault'} (≤ {FAULT_BOUND}); the dev "
                  f"fault named: {named}; readers {readers} (want ['video 4, audio 4'], 4 = "
                  f"cancelled); a file at the path: {exists}; {json.dumps(final)[:300]}")
    except (mcp.ToolError, KeyError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
        detail = f"{spec}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    finally:

                doc.close()
            except Exception:  # an instance that died is the row's FAIL already
                pass

def run_probe(sources):
    """P1–P5 and A1–A5: `webm_audio_probe.swift` built over `sources` and run."""
    import reference_build
    import swift_build
    out = WORK / ("probe" if Path(sources).resolve() == (ROOT / SOURCES).resolve()
                  else "probe-mutant")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = out / "main.swift"
    text = PROBE_SWIFT.read_text()
    if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text() != text:
        entry.write_text(text)
    binary, answer = out / "webm-audio-probe", out / "answer.json"
    defines = reference_build.tree_defines(Path(sources).parent.parent, ["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"])
    try:
        built = swift_build.build(sources=swift_build.app_sources(sources) + [entry],
                                  output=binary, defines=defines)
        if not built.reused:
            print(f"probe built in {built.seconds:.0f} s", flush=True)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        lines = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not build: "
                  + " | ".join(lines[:3] or list(error.diagnostics[:3]) or [str(error)]))
        return
    answer.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(answer)], 120)
    if ran["expired"] or ran["rc"] != 0 or not answer.exists():
        for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
            check(ident, False, "the probe did not run: "
                  + (ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]).strip()[-300:])
        return
    answered = {r["name"].split(" ")[0]: r for r in json.loads(answer.read_text())["rows"]}
    for ident in PROBE_ROWS:
        row = answered.get(ident)
        if row is None:
            check(ident, False, "the probe answered no such row")
        else:
            check(ident, row["ok"], f"{row['name'][len(ident) + 1:]}: {row['detail']}")

def run_probe_mutant(name):
    """A probe mutant: `app/Sources` copied with the anchor replaced, the probe alone."""
    import shutil
    mutant = MUTANTS[name]
    copy = WORK / "mutant-probe"
    shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
    sources = copy / "app" / "Sources"
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / SOURCES, sources)
    for path, anchor, replacement in mutant["anchors"]:
        target = copy / path
        text = target.read_text()
        if text.count(anchor) != 1:
            print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the anchor occurs "
                  f"{text.count(anchor)} times in {path}")
            return 2
        target.write_text(text.replace(anchor, replacement))
    try:
        run_probe(sources)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(copy, ignore_errors=True)
    failing = sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v)
    named = sorted(mutant["rows"])
    print(f"mutant {name}: named {named}, failing {failing}")
    if any(results.get(r) is None for r in PROBE_ROWS) or (
            failing == PROBE_ROWS and named != PROBE_ROWS):
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — the probe failed whole")
        return 2
    if named == failing:
        print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT: {name}")
        return 1
    if not set(named) & set(failing):
        print(f"MUTANT SURVIVED: {name}")
        return 0
    print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY: {name}")
    return 3


# ---- the mutants -------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_mutant(name):
    if name not in MUTANTS:
        print(f"unknown mutant {name}; the mutants are {sorted(MUTANTS)}")
        return 2
    mutant = MUTANTS[name]
    if mutant.get("probe"):
        return run_probe_mutant(name)
    named = list(mutant["rows"])
    print(f"mutant {name}: building the copy", flush=True)
    av1.MUTANTS = MUTANTS
    app, copy = av1.build_mutant(name)
    if app is None:
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {copy}")
        return 2
    cargo = mutant.get("cargo")
    if cargo:
        ran = bounded.run(["cargo", "test", "--release", "--no-fail-fast", "--test", cargo],
                          1200, cwd=str(copy / "core"))
        out = ran["stdout"] + ran["stderr"]
        if ran["expired"] or "test result:" not in out:
            print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — cargo rc {ran['rc']}: "
                  f"{out[-600:]}")
            return 2
        failed = re.findall(r"^test (\w+) \.\.\. FAILED$", out, re.M)
        check(f"cargo-{cargo}", ran["rc"] == 0, f"failed tests {failed}")
        named.append(f"cargo-{cargo}")
    logs = []
    try:
        if mutant.get("fault"):
            run_fault_rows(app, logs)
        else:
            run_rows(app, logs)
    except Exception as error:  # an instrument that cannot run is the control's failure
        print(f"mutant {name}: the control could not be performed — {error}")
        return 2
    failing = sorted(k for k, v in results.items() if not v)
    print(f"mutant {name}: named {sorted(named)}, failing {failing}")
    if sorted(named) == failing:
        print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT: {name}")
        return 1
    if not set(named) & set(failing):
        print(f"MUTANT SURVIVED: {name}")
        return 0
    print(f"MUTANT CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY: {name}")
    return 3


# ---- main --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_rows(app, logs):
    run_w_rows(app, logs)
    run_s4(app, logs)
    run_fault_rows(app, logs)
    run_probe(ROOT / SOURCES)
    run_readers_probe()
    found = [(i.label, line) for i in logs for line in i.complaints()]
    check("Z1", not found, f"{len(logs)} instance logs; complaints {found[:4]}")


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="the av1_webm row (codec-export C3)")
    parser.add_argument("--app", help="debug, release or a .app path (default RC_PROOF_APP)")
    parser.add_argument("--mutant", help="one of " + ", ".join(MUTANTS))
    parser.add_argument("--probe", action="store_true", help="the P and A rows alone, no app")
    parser.add_argument("--readers", action="store_true",
                        help="R1 alone: two readers against one, no app")
    parser.add_argument("--faults", action="store_true", help="F1–F3 alone, on the app")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.app:
        os.environ[proof_app.ENV] = args.app
    WORK.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if args.mutant:
        return run_mutant(args.mutant)
    if args.readers:
        run_readers_probe()
        print(f"scores: {sum(results.values())}/{len(results)}")
        return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1
    if args.probe:
        run_probe(ROOT / SOURCES)
        print(f"scores: {sum(results.values())}/{len(results)}")
        return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1
    logs = []
    try:
        app = proof_app.bundle()
        proof_app.require_fresh(proof_app.executable(app))
    except (proof_app.StaleApp, ValueError, OSError) as error:
        check("W0", False, f"the app cannot be driven: {error}")
        print("scores: 0/1")
        return 1
    print(f"app {app}", flush=True)
    if args.faults:
        run_fault_rows(app, logs)
        print(f"scores: {sum(results.values())}/{len(results)}")
        return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1
    run_rows(app, logs)
    passed = sum(results.values())
    print(f"scores: {passed}/{len(results)}")
    return 0 if all(results.values()) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
